newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin seeking cooperation with parliament, govt.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin seeking cooperation with parliament, govt.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, calling for cooperation between the Kremlin administration, the government and both houses of parliament, wants their chiefs to prepare key decisions together, his spokesman said on Monday.
"We must not run in different directions at this moment," spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as saying.

Yastrzhembsky told a Kremlin briefing that Yeltsin and Gennady Seleznyov, the communist speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament, had agreed that a new "permanent four" would meet regularly.

But there was no schedule yet for the meetings, between Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, Seleznyov and Yegor Stroyev, the speaker of the Federation Council upper chamber.
"In the current situation such meetings could become an effective mechanism to search for agreed solutions to the most important issues of the country's life," Yastrzhembsky said.

Yeltsin's proposal appeared aimed at seeking some form of cooperation between different branches of power while the 65-year-old preapares for heart surgery. It also follows the sacking of controversial security tsar Alexander Lebed.
